drawer.$comment: A panel docked to an edge of the window that the page goes on working around. It paints a surface for the dialog's reason and not the accordion's — a drawer arrives ON TOP of what was there, so it needs a background of its own, an edge and a shadow to sit above the page. What it does NOT have is a veil: there is no modality here, so there is no third token deciding how far the page behind is dimmed, and the panel's border is the only thing saying where it stops.
drawer.$comment-z-index: Below the CDK overlay container — the dependency's own number, read from its stylesheet by `check-tokens` on every run and held above this one (`layers.policy.json`): a select panel or a dialog opened from inside a drawer has to stand above it, and a drawer that climbed over its own content would be the toast's 1100 read backwards. It is a token and not a number in the sheet because an application with a layer of its own between the page and ours has nowhere else to say so.
drawer.$comment-panel-width: How far the panel reaches across the window when it is docked to the inline axis — and, by the same number, how far it travels to get there: the shut position is the open one pushed out by exactly this. `min(…, 100%)` in the sheet is what keeps a 320 px panel from overflowing a 280 px window.
drawer.$comment-panel-height: The block axis's half of the same decision. It is a separate token rather than one `size` because a sheet that reaches across the window wants a different measure from a column that reaches down it — a bottom sheet is short and wide, a side panel tall and narrow.

panel-gap.$description: Gap between the panel's heading and its content.

close-fg.$description: Text colour of the close button.

close-fg-hover.$description: Text colour of the close button on hover.

close-bg-hover.$description: Background of the close button on hover.

close-radius.$description: Corner radius of the close button.
